assumptions: The carcass is 645 mm tall: overall height 820 mm minus the 150 mm leg and the 25 mm top.
The three drawers sit in a row across the top of the unit with the two cupboard doors below - the sheet gives counts and a drawer front height but no layout.
Doors and drawer fronts are inset flush within the carcass openings, so the 1800 mm width and 450 mm depth include the front thickness.
A uniform 3 mm reveal is used between fronts and between fronts and carcass edges; this value is not stated.
The top is flush with the carcass sides and front (no overhang); if there is an overhang, the carcass shrinks by twice that amount.
The leg height of 150 mm is taken as floor to the underside of the carcass, and any levelling glide is assumed to sit recessed within it.
A rail frame (two long, two short) is assumed to tie the legs together beneath the carcass; the sheet does not describe the base.
The 18 mm 'carcass panel' figure is applied to the sides, bottom, dividers and fixed shelf.
Drawer boxes are assumed to be 12 mm solid oak sides and backs with a 6 mm base in grooves, on 400 mm metal side-mounted runners.
One adjustable shelf is assumed in each cupboard bay; the sheet does not mention shelving.
Pulls are assumed to be 160 mm bar handles in brass or steel, two hinges per door in the butt-hinge style, and four nylon levelling glides.

joints.notes: Each of the four legs receives one long and one short base rail; solid oak, so a haunched mortise and tenon at each leg.
Carcass bottom screwed down onto the rail frame.
Side panel to bottom panel; solid timber, dowelled or housed.
Back panel pinned and glued into a rebate around the rear of the carcass.
Fixed shelf dividing drawer bank from cupboard.
Vertical dividers fixed between carcass bottom and shelf, and between shelf and underside of top.
Top held down with figure-eight buttons or angle brackets so the oak can move.
Two hinges per door: outer door to side panel, inner stile side to the centre divider.
One pull per drawer front, through-bolted or screwed.
Runner bodies screwed to the carcass sides and the drawer-bay dividers.
Four corners per drawer box, three drawers.
Base panel floated in grooves in the sides and back.
Shelves resting on shelf pins in the side panel and divider.
Levelling foot pressed or screwed into the base of each leg.

object.style_notes: Solid oak sideboard in a plain contemporary/oak-furniture idiom: 60 x 60 mm square legs lifting a 645 mm carcass clear of the floor, three drawers in a row across the top over two cupboard doors below, 18 mm panels throughout, oiled finish with no applied decoration, plinth or visible metal frame.

readability.notes: Only page 1 of 2 was supplied and it is a text-only specification sheet: it lists dimensions but contains no drawing, photograph or view of the sideboard, so no part of the object is visible to crop. Every dimension used here therefore comes from the PDF text layer. No geometry, joinery or layout is shown, which is why several structural parts (leg rails, dividers, drawer boxes, hardware) are inferred from the stated overall size and typical sideboard construction. Page 2 may contain a drawing and should be checked before the model is finalised.
